hints: The pulley is at the bottom of the plane, so tension pulls P down the slope, meaning both tension $T = mg$ and weight component $mg\sin\alpha$ act down the slope.
Friction $F = \mu R$ opposes impending downward motion by acting up the slope: $F = mg\sin\alpha + T$.
walkthrough:
Given $\tan\alpha = \frac{7}{24}$, using a right-angled triangle with sides $7, 24, 25$:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25} = 0.28$$
$$\cos\alpha = \frac{24}{25} = 0.96$$

For particle P on the inclined plane, resolve forces perpendicular to the incline:
$$R = mg\cos\alpha = m(10)(0.96) = 9.6m$$

For hanging particle Q, vertical equilibrium gives:
$$T = mg = 10m$$
Because the pulley is positioned at the lower edge of the inclined plane, the string pulls particle P downwards along the slope.
The component of gravity down the slope also pulls P downwards: $mg\sin\alpha = m(10)(0.28) = 2.8m$.

Therefore, the impending motion of particle P is downwards, and limiting friction $F$ acts up the slope:
$$F = T + mg\sin\alpha = 10m + 2.8m = 12.8m$$

hints: With a force of $10\text{ N}$ applied up the slope, particle P accelerates up the slope at $a = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, pulling hanging particle Q upwards at $2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Write the equation of motion for Q: $T - mg = 2.5m \implies T = 12.5m$.
Friction on P opposes upward motion, acting down the slope: $F = \mu R = \frac{4}{3}(9.6m) = 12.8m$.
Write Newton's second law for P: $10 - mg\sin\alpha - F - T = 2.5m$, and solve for mass $m$.
walkthrough: When the $10\text{ N}$ force is applied up the incline, particle P accelerates up the plane at $a = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and particle Q accelerates upwards at $2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Write Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) for particle Q moving upwards:
$$T - m_Q g = m_Q a$$
$$T - 10m = 2.5m$$
$$T = 12.5m \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

For particle P moving up the incline, friction opposes the upward motion and acts down the slope:
$$F = \mu R = \frac{4}{3} \times 9.6m = 12.8m$$
The forces acting down the slope on P are the gravity component $mg\sin\alpha = 2.8m$, friction $F = 12.8m$, and tension $T$.

Write Newton's second law for particle P up the incline:
$$F_{\text{applied}} - mg\sin\alpha - F - T = m_P a$$
$$10 - 2.8m - 12.8m - T = 2.5m$$
$$10 - 15.6m - T = 2.5m \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$
